new_candidates.body:
Hi,

### Setup

- MuJoCo 3.15.0, Python bindings (PyPI wheel). Also reproduced with the nightly wheel 3.16.0.dev998671055 (from https://py.mujoco.org/), and with 3.12.0. 3.11.0 behaves differently (see below).
- macOS 27.0.1, arm64 (Apple Silicon), Python 3.12.13.
- Default options: `nativeccd` and `multiccd` enabled, zero margin.

### What's happening? What did you expect?

A compiled convex mesh can get a `mesh_polynormal` that points in the wrong direction. When that polygon is used by multiccd, the contact depth and normal are wrong.

In the model below, the plate is a 0.8 x 0.8 x 0.02 box-shaped mesh with one extra vertex 0.1 mm above the midpoint of one top edge. The top polygon's stored normal is `(0, -1, 0)`. Its outward normal is `(0, 0, 1)`. A 0.2 m box resting on the plate overlaps it by about 0.75 mm. With default flags, the reported contacts are 220 to 600 mm deep, and their normal is `(0, 1, 0)`.

Expected: about 0.75 mm depth with a vertical normal. This is what MuJoCo returns with multiccd disabled.

Dense convex hulls from automatic convex decomposition (e.g. CoACD) often have such nearly coplanar facets.

Output with 3.15.0 (full output in the collapsed section below):

```
polygon  stored normal (world)   Newell normal of its vertex loop (world)   vertices (world)
      5  [ 0. -1.  0.]   [0. 0. 1.]   [[0.4, 0.4, 0.01], [0.0, 0.4, 0.0101], [-0.4, 0.4, 0.01], [-0.4, -0.4, 0.01], [0.4, -0.4, 0.01]]   <-- wrong

default flags (nativeccd + multiccd)
  box at x=+0.00 y=+0.00: true vertical overlap 0.763 mm, mj_geomDistance -0.762 mm, ncon=2
    contact 0: dist  -500.000 mm   normal [0. 1. 0.]
    contact 1: dist  -500.000 mm   normal [0. 1. 0.]

multiccd disabled
  box at x=+0.00 y=+0.00: true vertical overlap 0.763 mm, mj_geomDistance -0.762 mm, ncon=1
    contact 0: dist    -0.762 mm   normal [ 0.  0. -1.]
```

**Why this looks like a defect rather than intended behavior**

1. *The input is a valid convex mesh that MuJoCo itself treats as one planar face.* The top triangles differ by about 0.014°, well inside `kAngleTol` (0.01 rad, about 0.57°), so `MakePolygons` puts them in one polygon (polygon 5 in the output) ([L2770-L2821](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/blob/3.15.0/src/user/user_mesh.cc#L2770-L2821)).
2. *MuJoCo already has the correct normal and then overwrites it.* `MakePolygons` stores the group's direction, which is within the grouping tolerance of every member triangle ([L2811-L2813](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/blob/3.15.0/src/user/user_mesh.cc#L2811-L2813)). After the vertices are re-centered and rotated, `MakePolygonNormals` replaces it with the normal of the first three outline vertices ([L1471-L1472](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/blob/3.15.0/src/user/user_mesh.cc#L1471-L1472), [L2518-L2529](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/blob/3.15.0/src/user/user_mesh.cc#L2518-L2529)). The repro prints the stored normal `(0, -1, 0)` next to the outline's own outward normal `(0, 0, 1)`.
3. *The result contradicts MuJoCo's own distance query for the same pair and pose.* `mj_geomDistance` returns -0.762 mm, while the multiccd contacts report -220 to -600 mm with a sideways normal (repro output below). The multicontact result replaces the EPA result ([L1691-L1732](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/blob/3.15.0/src/engine/engine_collision_gjk.c#L1691-L1732)).
4. *A fix has no runtime cost and no behavioral trade-off.* Polygon normals are computed once at compile time. Keeping the grouped normal (rotated with the vertices) or using Newell's method over the full outline gives the same result as today for exactly planar polygons, and only changes polygons whose first three vertices are nearly collinear. Replacing `mesh_polynormal` with Newell normals at runtime restores correct contacts in the repro.

**Cause.** The first three outline vertices of the top polygon are `(0.4, 0.4, 0.01)`, `(0, 0.4, 0.0101)` and `(-0.4, 0.4, 0.01)`. In the plane they lie on one straight edge, and the middle one is 0.1 mm higher. A normal computed from these three points alone therefore lies in the plane of that edge. Here it comes out horizontal, `(0, -1, 0)`.

- [`mjCMesh::MakePolygons`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/blob/3.15.0/src/user/user_mesh.cc#L2770-L2821) groups hull triangles by a quantized normal direction (`kAngleTol = 0.01`). It stores the bin's direction as the polygon normal ([L2795-L2797](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/blob/3.15.0/src/user/user_mesh.cc#L2795-L2797), [L2606-L2608](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/blob/3.15.0/src/user/user_mesh.cc#L2606-L2608), [L2811-L2813](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/blob/3.15.0/src/user/user_mesh.cc#L2811-L2813)). This direction is close to the normal of every triangle in the group.
- The vertices are then moved to the center of mass and rotated ([L1454-L1460](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/blob/3.15.0/src/user/user_mesh.cc#L1454-L1460)).
- After that, [`mjCMesh::MakePolygonNormals`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/blob/3.15.0/src/user/user_mesh.cc#L2518-L2529) (called at [L1471-L1472](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/blob/3.15.0/src/user/user_mesh.cc#L1471-L1472)) replaces each normal with `mjuu_makenormal(polygon[0], polygon[1], polygon[2])`. This uses only the first three outline vertices. On hulls with many nearly coplanar facets and extra vertices close to straight edges, these three vertices can be nearly collinear. The result is then dominated by small out-of-plane offsets, as in this example.

In multicontact, the stored normals decide which polygons are paired ([`alignedFaces`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/blob/3.15.0/src/engine/engine_collision_gjk.c#L2136-L2152), tolerance `mjFACE_TOL`). They are also used inside [`polygonClip`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/blob/3.15.0/src/engine/engine_collision_gjk.c#L1601-L1733), whose output replaces the EPA result:

- the clipping planes ([`planeNormal`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/blob/3.15.0/src/engine/engine_collision_gjk.c#L1568-L1579));
- the depth of each point ([`witnessOnFace`](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/blob/3.15.0/src/engine/engine_collision_gjk.c#L1590-L1597));
- the witness direction, which becomes the contact normal ([L2354-L2356](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/blob/3.15.0/src/engine/engine_collision_gjk.c#L2354-L2356)).

My reading of the code is that, in this example, the plate's top polygon is paired with a box face whose normal is anti-parallel to the wrong stored normal, and depth is measured along that face. I have not instrumented this; it is consistent with the output.

**Version history.** Commit 17e6d44a2 ("Support variable accurate contact depth in multicontact", in 3.12.0) changed multicontact to compute the depth of each point from the polygon normal. Before that commit, every point copied the EPA depth. The same commit also loosened `mjFACE_TOL` from about 0.09° to about 5.1°. I see this change in the repro:

- 3.11.0: the stored normal is already wrong. The contacts have the correct depth (-0.762 mm) but the sideways normal `(0, 1, 0)`.
- 3.12.0, 3.15.0 and the nightly: the depth is also wrong (-220 to -600 mm).

**Workaround check.** Replacing every `mesh_polynormal` at runtime with the Newell normal of the polygon's own vertex loop restores 4 contacts with a vertical normal. Their depth is -0.700 mm, against a true overlap of 0.73 to 0.76 mm. I think the remaining ~0.06 mm comes from the polygon not being exactly planar (its vertices span 0.1 mm), but I have not checked this in detail.

**Suggested fix:** compute each polygon normal in `MakePolygonNormals` with Newell's method, i.e. the normalized vector area of the full outline loop (sum of the cross products of a triangle fan), keeping the current `(1, 0, 0)` fallback only for a zero-area loop. It uses the loop's winding, so it stays outward after the negative-scale winding reversal added for #3604. The workaround check above is this computation done at runtime.

Reusing the grouped normal from `MakePolygons` (rotated with the vertices) is not a good alternative: it is quantized to the `kAngleTol = 0.01` rad grid of the grouping key, so it would tilt the normals of exactly planar faces by up to half a grid step (about 0.005 rad in each of the two angles).

**Related, but different:**
- #3604: negative mesh scale produced inward polygon normals. Fixed before 3.15.0. This repro uses no scaling.
- #3654: multiccd reversed the EPA normal when an edge clip produced no points. That bug keeps the depth. The fix is on main, and this repro still fails on the nightly wheel.

### Steps for reproduction

1. Save the script below as `repro.py`. The model is inlined.
2. Run `python repro.py`.
3. Polygon 5, the plate's top face, prints a stored normal of `(0, -1, 0)` instead of `(0, 0, 1)`. With default flags, the contacts are hundreds of mm deep with normal `(0, 1, 0)`. With multiccd disabled, they are about 0.76 mm deep and vertical.

### Minimal model for reproduction

<details>
<summary>minimal XML</summary>

```XML
<mujoco>
  <asset>
    <mesh name="plate" vertex="-0.4 -0.4  0.01    0.4 -0.4  0.01    0.4 0.4  0.01   -0.4 0.4  0.01
                               0    0.4  0.0101
                              -0.4 -0.4 -0.01     0.4 -0.4 -0.01    0.4 0.4 -0.01   -0.4 0.4 -0.01"/>
  </asset>
  <worldbody>
    <geom name="plate" type="mesh" mesh="plate"/>
    <body name="box" pos="0 0 0.1093">
      <freejoint/>
      <geom name="box" type="box" size="0.1 0.1 0.1"/>
    </body>
  </worldbody>
</mujoco>
```
</details>

### Code required for reproduction

<details>
<summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
"""Wrong mesh_polynormal on a nearly flat convex face -> deep, sideways multiccd contact.

Plate: 0.8 x 0.8 x 0.02 box-shaped mesh, plus ONE extra vertex 0.1 mm above the midpoint
of the top edge at y = +0.4. Box: 0.2 m cube resting on the plate with ~0.75 mm overlap.
"""
import numpy as np
import mujoco

XML = """
<mujoco>
  <asset>
    <mesh name="plate" vertex="-0.4 -0.4  0.01    0.4 -0.4  0.01    0.4 0.4  0.01   -0.4 0.4  0.01
                               0    0.4  0.0101
                              -0.4 -0.4 -0.01     0.4 -0.4 -0.01    0.4 0.4 -0.01   -0.4 0.4 -0.01"/>
  </asset>
  <worldbody>
    <geom name="plate" type="mesh" mesh="plate"/>
    <body name="box" pos="0 0 0.1093">
      <freejoint/>
      <geom name="box" type="box" size="0.1 0.1 0.1"/>
    </body>
  </worldbody>
</mujoco>
"""

model = mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_string(XML)
data = mujoco.MjData(model)
print("MuJoCo", mujoco.__version__)

# --- 1. stored polygon normal vs. the outward normal of the same vertex loop -----------------
mujoco.mj_forward(model, data)
g = model.geom("plate").id
R = data.geom_xmat[g].reshape(3, 3)
mesh = model.mesh("plate").id
vert = model.mesh_vert[model.mesh_vertadr[mesh]:][:model.mesh_vertnum[mesh]].astype(float)
newell_normals = {}
print("\npolygon  stored normal (world)   Newell normal of its vertex loop (world)   vertices (world)")
for p in range(model.mesh_polyadr[mesh], model.mesh_polyadr[mesh] + model.mesh_polynum[mesh]):
  ids = model.mesh_polyvert[model.mesh_polyvertadr[p]:][:model.mesh_polyvertnum[p]]
  P = vert[ids]
  Q = np.roll(P, -1, axis=0)
  newell = np.array([np.sum((P[:, 1] - Q[:, 1]) * (P[:, 2] + Q[:, 2])),
                     np.sum((P[:, 2] - Q[:, 2]) * (P[:, 0] + Q[:, 0])),
                     np.sum((P[:, 0] - Q[:, 0]) * (P[:, 1] + Q[:, 1]))])
  newell /= np.linalg.norm(newell)
  newell_normals[p] = newell
  stored = R @ model.mesh_polynormal[p]
  flag = "   <-- wrong" if stored @ (R @ newell) < 0.99 else ""
  world = P @ R.T + data.geom_xpos[g]
  print(f"{p:7d}  {np.round(stored, 3) + 0.0}   {np.round(R @ newell, 3) + 0.0}   "
        f"{(np.round(world, 4) + 0.0).tolist()}{flag}")

# --- 2. contacts for a few resting poses, with and without multiccd ---------------------------
def top_z(x, y):
  # height of the plate's top surface (convex hull of the 5 top vertices) at (x, y)
  tri = [((-0.4, -0.4, 0.01), (0.4, -0.4, 0.01), (0.0, 0.4, 0.0101)),
         ((-0.4, -0.4, 0.01), (0.0, 0.4, 0.0101), (-0.4, 0.4, 0.01)),
         ((0.4, -0.4, 0.01), (0.4, 0.4, 0.01), (0.0, 0.4, 0.0101))]
  z = []
  for a, b, c in tri:
    n = np.cross(np.subtract(b, a), np.subtract(c, a))
    z.append(a[2] - (n[0] * (x - a[0]) + n[1] * (y - a[1])) / n[2])
  return min(z)  # convex roof: the lowest of the supporting planes

poses = [(0.0, 0.0), (-0.28, -0.28), (0.25, 0.1)]
zc = 0.1093  # box centre height: box bottom at z = 0.0093
def patch_normals():
  # replace every stored polygon normal by the Newell normal of its own vertex loop
  for p, n in newell_normals.items():
    model.mesh_polynormal[p] = n

for label, flags, patch in (("default flags (nativeccd + multiccd)", 0, False),
                            ("multiccd disabled", int(mujoco.mjtDisableBit.mjDSBL_MULTICCD), False),
                            ("default flags, mesh_polynormal replaced by Newell normals", 0, True)):
  model.opt.disableflags = flags
  if patch:
    patch_normals()
  print(f"\n{label}")
  for x, y in poses:
    data.qpos[:7] = [x, y, zc, 1, 0, 0, 0]
    mujoco.mj_forward(model, data)
    s = np.linspace(-0.1, 0.1, 41)
    overlap = max(top_z(x + u, y + v) for u in s for v in s) - (zc - 0.1)
    dist = mujoco.mj_geomDistance(model, data, g, model.geom("box").id, 0.1, None)
    print(f"  box at x={x:+.2f} y={y:+.2f}: true vertical overlap {overlap * 1000:.3f} mm, "
          f"mj_geomDistance {dist * 1000:.3f} mm, ncon={data.ncon}")
    for i in range(data.ncon):
      c = data.contact[i]
      print(f"    contact {i}: dist {c.dist * 1000:9.3f} mm   normal {np.round(c.frame[:3], 3) + 0.0}")
```
</details>

```
      1  [-1.  0.  0.]   [-1.  0.  0.]   [[-0.4, 0.4, -0.01], [-0.4, -0.4, -0.01], [-0.4, -0.4, 0.01], [-0.4, 0.4, 0.01]]

      3  [ 0. -1.  0.]   [ 0. -1.  0.]   [[0.4, -0.4, -0.01], [0.4, -0.4, 0.01], [-0.4, -0.4, 0.01], [-0.4, -0.4, -0.01]]

      5  [ 0. -1.  0.]   [0. 0. 1.]   [[0.4, 0.4, 0.01], [0.0, 0.4, 0.0101], [-0.4, 0.4, 0.01], [-0.4, -0.4, 0.01], [0.4, -0.4, 0.01]]   <-- wrong

    contact 0: dist    -0.762 mm   normal [ 0.  0. -1.]
  box at x=-0.28 y=-0.28: true vertical overlap 0.728 mm, mj_geomDistance -0.727 mm, ncon=1
    contact 0: dist    -0.727 mm   normal [ 0.  0. -1.]
  box at x=+0.25 y=+0.10: true vertical overlap 0.763 mm, mj_geomDistance -0.762 mm, ncon=1
    contact 0: dist    -0.762 mm   normal [ 0.  0. -1.]

default flags, mesh_polynormal replaced by Newell normals
  box at x=+0.00 y=+0.00: true vertical overlap 0.763 mm, mj_geomDistance -0.762 mm, ncon=4
    contact 0: dist    -0.700 mm   normal [ 0.  0. -1.]
    contact 1: dist    -0.700 mm   normal [ 0.  0. -1.]
    contact 2: dist    -0.700 mm   normal [ 0.  0. -1.]
    contact 3: dist    -0.700 mm   normal [ 0.  0. -1.]
  box at x=-0.28 y=-0.28: true vertical overlap 0.728 mm, mj_geomDistance -0.727 mm, ncon=4
    contact 0: dist    -0.700 mm   normal [ 0.  0. -1.]
    contact 1: dist    -0.700 mm   normal [ 0.  0. -1.]
    contact 2: dist    -0.700 mm   normal [ 0.  0. -1.]
    contact 3: dist    -0.700 mm   normal [ 0.  0. -1.]
  box at x=+0.25 y=+0.10: true vertical overlap 0.763 mm, mj_geomDistance -0.762 mm, ncon=4
    contact 0: dist    -0.700 mm   normal [ 0.  0. -1.]
    contact 1: dist    -0.700 mm   normal [ 0.  0. -1.]
    contact 2: dist    -0.700 mm   normal [ 0.  0. -1.]
    contact 3: dist    -0.700 mm   normal [ 0.  0. -1.]
```
</details>

The nightly wheel 3.16.0.dev998671055 and 3.12.0 give identical output. With 3.11.0, the stored normal is the same; the default-flags contacts are 4 points at -0.762 / -0.727 mm with normal `(0, 1, 0)`.

### Confirmations

- [x] I searched the [latest documentation](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/latest/overview.html) thoroughly before posting.
- [x] I searched previous [Issues](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/issues) and [Discussions](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/discussions), I am certain this has not been raised before.
new_candidates.title: Mesh polygon normal computed from three nearly collinear outline vertices; multiccd then returns a deep contact with a sideways normal
